You are porting src/misc.c to idiomatic Zig (src/misc.zig) in this repository (zelda3: a reverse-engineered C reimplementation of The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past, currently mid-way through an incremental C-to-Zig port at behavioral parity, verified by a RAM-compare oracle against the original ROM). This is backlog task TASK-004.06.

## Goal
Port `src/misc.c` (960 lines), containing `Module_MainRouting` — the top-level game-state dispatcher called every frame from `ZeldaRunGameLoop` — to `src/misc.zig`, matching C-ABI symbols exactly so the remaining .c callers link unchanged. This is a deeply interconnected core file (18 includes: variables.h, hud.h, dungeon.h, overworld.h, load_gfx.h, sprite.h, poly.h, ancilla.h, select_file.h, tile_detect.h, player.h, player_oam.h, messaging.h, ending.h, attract.h, snes/snes_regs.h, assets.h) — go carefully and re-verify parity thoroughly given how central Module_MainRouting is.

## Public C-ABI surface to preserve exactly (from src/misc.h)
Functions (extern "C", exact names/signatures, called by other .c files that must link unchanged):
SrcPtr, Ancilla_Sfx2_Near, Ancilla_Sfx3_Near, LoadDungeonRoomRebuildHUD, Module_Unknown0, Module_Unknown1,
Module_MainRouting, NMI_PrepareSprites, Sound_LoadIntroSongBank, LoadOverworldSongs, LoadDungeonSongs,
LoadCreditsSongs, Dungeon_LightTorch, RoomDraw_AdjustTorchLightingChange, Dungeon_PrepOverlayDma_nextPrep,
Dungeon_PrepOverlayDma_watergate, Module05_LoadFile, Module13_BossVictory_Pendant, BossVictory_Heal,
Dungeon_StartVictorySpin, Dungeon_RunVictorySpin, Dungeon_CloseVictorySpin, Module15_MirrorWarpFromAga,
Module16_BossVictory_Crystal, Module16_04_FadeAndEnd, TriforceRoom_LinkApproachTriforce,
AncillaAdd_ItemReceipt, ItemReceipt_GiveBottledItem, Module17_SaveAndQuit,
WallMaster_SendPlayerToLastEntrance, GetRandomNumber, Link_CalculateSfxPan, SpriteSfx_QueueSfx1WithPan,
SpriteSfx_QueueSfx2WithPan, SpriteSfx_QueueSfx3WithPan, Sprite_CalculateSfxPan, CalculateSfxPan,
CalculateSfxPan_Arbitrary, Init_LoadDefaultTileAttr, Main_ShowTextMessage, HandleItemTileAction_Overworld

Data symbol: `extern const uint16 kMemoryLocationToGiveItemTo[76];` — defined in misc.c (line 60), must be
re-exported from misc.zig as an extern "C" const array with identical layout/values (other .c files
read it by name).

Two header-only static-inline helpers (`GetOamCurPtr`, `FindInByteArray`, `FindInWordArray`) live in
misc.h itself, not misc.c — they are NOT linked symbols and do not need porting/exporting. If misc.zig
needs equivalent logic internally, reimplement it Zig-natively (see the existing pattern in
src/player_oam.zig, which already has its own private zig-idiomatic FindInByteArray using slices
instead of a separate size param — do the same rather than trying to call the C header inline).

## Established port pattern — study these first
- `src/player_oam.zig` — most recently completed port (TASK-004.05), same file scale/style: header
  comment explaining what it ports and the C-ABI/RAM-compare contract, `const t = @import("types.zig")`,
  `const v = @import("variables.zig")` for g_ram access, `extern "C" fn` for every exported symbol,
  `extern const ... : [N]t.uintN` for shared data, inline helpers for repeated C macros
  (e.g. features0 flag checks via direct g_ram byte access since C-only macros aren't in variables.zig).
- `build.zig`:
  - Line ~496: the static `sources` array still lists `"src/misc.c"` — remove this line once misc.zig
    is complete and wired in (matches how player_oam.c was dropped from `sources` when player_oam.zig
    landed — note player_oam.c is still kept on disk as a reference/backup, just removed from the build).
  - Line ~48: add `exe.root_module.addObjectFile(addPortedModule(b, target, optimize, "misc"));` in the
    same list as the other ported modules (config, spc_player, poly, tile_detect, load_gfx, nmi,
    overlord, player_oam, ...) — `addPortedModule` (build.zig:144) wires `src/<name>.zig` in
    automatically; no other build.zig change needed.
- Look at a few other already-ported modules for variety of idiom (e.g. overlord.zig, load_gfx.zig,
  nmi.zig) especially ones that touch sprites/HUD/dungeon state similar to what misc.c touches.

## Steps
1. Read src/misc.c and src/misc.h fully. Read the 18 included headers as needed to understand the
   types and cross-module calls misc.c makes (you are not porting those modules — only calling into
   their still-C or already-ported-Zig APIs exactly as misc.c does today).
2. Read 2-3 existing ported .zig modules (player_oam.zig at minimum, plus 1-2 more) to internalize the
   house style: extern "C" export style, g_ram access via variables.zig accessors, types.zig aliases,
   comment conventions.
3. Write src/misc.zig porting every function and the data symbol above, preserving exact C-ABI names,
   signatures, and behavior (byte-for-byte where the original 65816 code and the RAM-compare oracle
   expect it — no behavioral "improvements").
4. Update build.zig: remove `"src/misc.c"` from `sources` (~line 496), add the `addPortedModule(...,
   "misc")` wiring call (~line 48, alongside the other ported modules).
5. Build and verify (from repo root):
   - `task zig:build` — must compile clean.
   - `task zig:ast-check` — quick source-only check.
   - `task zig:parity` — runs the Zig-built binary against zelda3.sfc and reports RAM-compare pass/fail.
     Zero "Memory compare failed" lines on stderr is the bar.
   - `task zig:parity-replay` — replays every saves/ref/Chapter*.sav reference save under headless
     Wayland and fails on any RAM-compare mismatch across overworld/dungeon/menus. Run this too before
     declaring done — it's the strongest signal for a file this central.
6. If parity fails, diagnose against the original src/misc.c (still on disk, unmodified — do NOT
   remove or edit misc.c's content, only stop compiling it) and fix misc.zig. Iterate until clean or
   until you've made your best-effort attempt and are genuinely stuck — in that case, stop and report
   exactly what's failing (which function, which save/state, what the RAM-compare diff shows) rather
   than declaring success prematurely.

## Definition of Done
- `task zig:build` compiles clean.
- Zero "Memory compare failed" lines on stderr with zelda3.sfc loaded (task zig:parity).
- saves/ref/Chapter*.sav replay stays clean (task zig:parity-replay).
- misc.zig's exported C-ABI symbols are unchanged so remaining .c files link without edits.
- zelda3.bak and the C taskfile.yml build remain untouched and working (don't touch anything under
  taskfile.yml's C build path — only build.zig / taskfiles/zig.yml concerns you here).

Do not mark this done unless the parity gate is actually green. If you plateau short of full parity,
report precisely where it breaks so a human can pick up from there.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://taskfile.dev/schema.json

version: "3.0"

vars:
  ZIG_BIN: zig-out/bin/zelda3

tasks:
  build:
    desc: Compile the zelda3 binary via build.zig (parity with `task build`)
    sources:
      - build.zig
      - build.zig.zon
      - src/**/*.c
      - src/**/*.h
      - snes/**/*.c
      - snes/**/*.h
    generates:
      - "{{.ZIG_BIN}}"
    cmds:
      - zig build

  run:
    desc: Build and run the Zig-built zelda3 binary
    deps: [build]
    cmds:
      - zig build run

  clean:
    desc: Remove Zig build artifacts (zig-out/, .zig-cache/)
    cmds:
      - rm -rf zig-out .zig-cache

  parity:
    desc: Run the Zig-built binary against zelda3.sfc and report RAM-compare pass/fail
    deps:
      - task: build
      - task: :assets
    cmds:
      - |
        set +e
        LOG="$(mktemp)"
        timeout 10s "{{.ZIG_BIN}}" zelda3.sfc >"$LOG" 2>&1
        status=$?
        if [ "$status" -ne 0 ] && [ "$status" -ne 124 ]; then
          echo "zelda3 exited with status $status" >&2
          cat "$LOG" >&2
          rm -f "$LOG"
          exit 1
        fi
        if grep -q "Memory compare failed" "$LOG"; then
          echo "PARITY FAILED: RAM-compare mismatches detected" >&2
          grep "Memory compare failed" "$LOG" >&2
          rm -f "$LOG"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "PARITY OK: zero RAM-compare mismatches"
        rm -f "$LOG"

  test:
    desc: Run Tier-A unit tests for ported Zig modules (zig build test); no-op until a module exists
    sources:
      - build.zig
      - build.zig.zon
      - src/**/*.zig
      - snes/**/*.zig
    cmds:
      - zig build test

  difftest:
    desc: Run Tier-B differential tests (C-vs-Zig behavioral equivalence) for ported Zig modules; no-op until a module exists
    sources:
      - build.zig
      - build.zig.zon
      - src/**/*.zig
      - snes/**/*.zig
    cmds:
      - zig build difftest

  ast-check:
    desc: Run `zig ast-check` over every ported .zig file (fast, source-only; no type-checking or build)
    cmds:
      - find src snes -name '*.zig' -print0 | xargs -0 {{.ROOT_DIR}}/scripts/zig-ast-check.sh

  parity-replay:
    desc: Replay every saves/ref/Chapter*.sav reference save under headless Wayland (sway+wtype+grim) and fail on any RAM-compare mismatch
    platforms: [linux]
    deps:
      - task: build
      - task: :assets
      - task: :playtest:linux
    vars:
      REPLAY_SECONDS: '{{.REPLAY_SECONDS | default "12"}}'
    cmds:
      - |
        set +e
        WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)"
        INI="$WORKDIR/zelda3-verify.ini"
        sed -e "s/^#LoadRef = /LoadRef = /" -e "s/^#ReplayRef = /ReplayRef = /" zelda3.ini > "$INI"

        SWAY_CONF="$WORKDIR/zelda-sway.conf"
        LOG="$WORKDIR/zelda-verify.log"
        cat > "$SWAY_CONF" <<EOF
        output HEADLESS-1 resolution 1024x896
        exec sh -c "cd {{.ROOT_DIR}} && exec env SDL_VIDEODRIVER=wayland SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy ./{{.ZIG_BIN}} --config $INI zelda3.sfc" > $LOG 2>&1
        EOF

        pkill -9 -x zelda3 2>/dev/null
        pkill -9 -x sway 2>/dev/null
        pkill -9 -x wtype 2>/dev/null
        sleep 1

        setsid nohup env WLR_BACKENDS=headless WLR_RENDERER=pixman sway -c "$SWAY_CONF" >"$WORKDIR/sway.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
        sleep 3

        SOCK="$(ls "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"/wayland-[0-9]* 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
